pr_title: Console Logging for StrictMode Double Rendering
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/facebook/react/issues/21889.

React currently suppress console logs in StrictMode during double rendering. However, this causes a lot of confusion. This PR moves the console suppression logic from React into React Devtools. Now by default, we no longer suppress console logs. Instead, we gray out the logs in console during double render. We also add a setting in React Devtools to allow developers to hide console logs during double render if they choose.

 - [x] Disable console suppression by default in React.
 - [x] Add an API for DevTools and React to communicate about when double rendering (or lifecycles) start and stop.
 - [x] DevTools should gray out (but not hide) logs during second render pass by default.
 - [x] DevTools should expose a new Debugging preference that allows users to suppress second logs entirely (mimicking the current default behavior).

issue_context.title: [DevTools] Console logging and StrictMode double rendering
issue_context.body:
React currently suppress all console logs while double rendering (or double invoking render phase lifecycles) to reduce console noise, e.g.:
https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/310187264d01a31bc3079358f13662d31a079d9e/packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberBeginWork.new.js#L366-L384

Unfortunately this often causes confusion and leads to complaints (see the discussion on #21783). We could leverage DevTools to improve the default experience and give developers control over this behavior.

- [ ] Disable console suppression by default in React.
- [ ] Add an API for DevTools and React to communicate about when double rendering (or lifecycles) start and stop.
- [ ] DevTools should gray out (but not hide) logs during second render pass by default.
- [ ] DevTools should expose a new Debugging preference that allows users to suppress second logs entirely (mimicking the current default behavior).

DevTools targets newer browsers. ReactDOM needs to support much older ones.

The one exception is the standalone DevTools _backend_ because Hermes lacks a lot of ES6 support (although I've raised a request with them to add more).

Extra context:

By default, all DevTools build targets share this common Babel configuration:
https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/5634ed16aaba4a507844f0502953abcf40e3a165/packages/react-devtools-shared/babel.config.js#L19-L26

https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/5634ed16aaba4a507844f0502953abcf40e3a165/packages/react-devtools-extensions/chrome/manifest.json#L8

And Firefox:
https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/5634ed16aaba4a507844f0502953abcf40e3a165/packages/react-devtools-extensions/firefox/manifest.json#L10

Both of which are new enough not to require this polyfill you mention.

We override this for Hermes here by targeting IE11 (which has the same lack of support for ES6):
https://github.com/facebook/react/blob/c5cfa71948dbf4c2dd9ff64596ab663f8d559cd6/packages/react-devtools-core/webpack.backend.js#L21-L24
